newsitem.title: MEXICO: Televisa still down on chairman's health.
newsitem.headline: Televisa still down on chairman's health.

text.p: Grupo Televisa SA de CV shares were down at midday trade on Friday for the second day in a row on news of the media group chairman's ill health, traders and analysts said.

"They're still down on news that the chairman is ill. Televisa has a reputation of being a one-man company, so any management changeover, even if it's only temporary, is a cause for concern," a desk trader said.
Televisa L shares were down 2.90 pesos at 100.90 pesos in mid-afternoon on Friday, while its ADRs were off 7/8 at 25-3/4 on Wall Street.
Televisa announced on Thursday that Chairman Emilio Azcarraga Milmo -- known as "The Tiger" -- had taken leave of absence from his normal duties for medical care in Los Angeles.

The company also said Chief Operating Officer Emilio Azcarraga Jean would in The Tiger's absence take over broadcasting operations, while Guillermo Canedo White, executive vice president and chief financial officer, would take over corporate and administrative affairs.
Televisa is the world's largest producer of television programs in Spanish.
An analyst from Arka brokerage in Mexico City, who asked not to be named, said changes in the Televisa board line-up were on the agenda for an assembly of holders of preferential A shares on March 4.
"The meeting means there is at least the possibility that management changes may become permament, that Mr. Azcarraga will play a less active role," the analyst said.

"The current replacements have been in the business all their lives and there's no reason why the company should not run smoothly in their hands, but changeovers always worry the markets," the analyst added.
